class.name: NNNQSSearchSpaces
class.brief_description: Defines the set of nodes that will be included in the search when a query is executed.
class.description: The search space nodes are used to define the set of nodes that will be included in the search when a query is executed. The search space nodes need to have [NNNQSSearchCriteria] nodes as their children. When the query finishes, the search spaces emit the [signal query_completed] signal. The search spaces fill in a TypedArray [member query_results] and a PackedFloat64Array [member query_result_scores]. These are sorted by the score in a descending order. This means that the first node in the [member query_results] array is also the one with the highest score. The [method execute_query] method average runtime and other metrics (see below) are available for debugging and finetuning your queries. Each search space can be run by itself, by calling its [method execute_query] method until it returns [code]true[/code] (completed), or by using the [code]NodeQuerySystem[/code] singleton. If the singleton is used, you should not use the [method execute_query] method at all, but simply post the query using [method NNNodeQuerySystem.post_query] instead. The [code]NodeQuerySystem[/code] singleton is the recommended way of executing the queries for search spaces, as it allows the use of time budgeting.

method.name: execute_query
method.description: The [method execute_query] method fetches the search space nodes based on its configuration and then applies the search criteria in top-down order. [param time_budget_usec] limits the time, in microseconds, this call spends on the query; a query that runs out of time resumes where it left off on the next call. A budget of [code]0[/code] runs the query to completion in this call. Returns [code]false[/code] if the query hasn't finished (time has run out) and [code]true[/code] otherwise.

method.name: get_debug_scored_nodes
method.description: Debug builds only. Every candidate that survived the search criteria in the last completed query, in search-space order. Empty unless the search space is being watched with [method watch_debug_scores]. Unlike [member query_results] this is not limited to the top [member top_n_to_find] nodes.

method.name: get_debug_scored_scores
method.description: Debug builds only. The final scores of the nodes returned by [method get_debug_scored_nodes], index for index.

method.name: initialize_search_space
method.description: Runs the search space's internal initialization (for example, generating point-grid nodes or connecting area signals). This is called automatically from the native [method Node._ready] implementation. If a script attached to this node overrides [method Node._ready], the native [method Node._ready] will not run and you must call [method initialize_search_space] yourself.

method.name: unwatch_debug_scores
method.description: Debug builds only. Releases one [method watch_debug_scores] call. Recording stops, and the copies returned by [method get_debug_scored_nodes] and [method get_debug_scored_scores] are cleared, when the last watcher releases its call.

method.name: watch_debug_scores
method.description: Debug builds only. Starts copying every surviving candidate and its final score, as returned by [method get_debug_scored_nodes] and [method get_debug_scored_scores], when a query completes. This lets the debugger draw all scored points instead of only the top [member top_n_to_find] results. Calls are reference counted, so several watchers can watch the same search space; each one must pair its call with [method unwatch_debug_scores]. The copy costs time proportional to the search space size on every completed query, so watch only while something is inspecting the query.

members.member: Average duration in microseconds of a single [method execute_query] call for the latest completed query. Read-only runtime state: never saved with the scene.
Duration in microseconds spent handling the [signal query_completed] signal (your result-handling listeners). Read-only runtime state: never saved with the scene.
Duration in microseconds of the latest [method execute_query] call. Read-only runtime state: never saved with the scene.

Whether a query is currently in progress. Set to [code]true[/code] when posted with [method NNNodeQuerySystem.post_query] and to [code]false[/code] when it completes or is stopped with [method NNNodeQuerySystem.stop_query]. Read-only runtime state: never saved with the scene.

If [code]true[/code], after each criterion evaluates a candidate node, the search space calls [method Object.set] on that node to write [code]is_filtered[/code] ([bool], whether the criterion filtered it out) and [code]score[/code] ([float], the node's accumulated score so far). This does not create new properties; the candidate node (or its script) must already define those properties for the values to be stored.
Scores of the nodes in [member query_results], index for index, sorted highest first. Read-only runtime state: never saved with the scene.
Surviving candidate nodes from the latest completed query, sorted in descending order by score, up to [member top_n_to_find] entries. Read-only runtime state: never saved with the scene.
Duration in microseconds spent fetching the candidate nodes before filtering and scoring. Read-only runtime state: never saved with the scene.
Maximum number of highest-scoring nodes returned in [member query_results]. Must be at least [code]1[/code]; smaller values are rejected with an error.
Number of [method execute_query] calls taken to finish the latest query. Read-only runtime state: never saved with the scene.
Total number of candidate node evaluations performed across all criteria for the latest query. Read-only runtime state: never saved with the scene.

Total time in microseconds spent inside [method execute_query] calls to complete the latest query. Multi-frame queries sum the runtime of each call, not the wall-clock time between them. Read-only runtime state: never saved with the scene.

signal.name: query_completed
signal.description: Emitted when the query execution is completed. [param search_space] is this [NNNQSSearchSpaces] node, whose [member query_results] and [member query_result_scores] hold the completed results.
